title: System Then People
summary: Raw explanation → AI SOP → test twice → then hire or delegate

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Introduction
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What Will You Understand? People perform better when the system is clear first — and AI transforms your explanation into a simple SOP (Standard Operating Procedure).
- Why Now? After you’ve organized your work and considered delegation, hiring without a system increases chaos.
- What After the Lesson? You will write a raw process and ask AI to convert it into an SOP outline — and review it.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- A new employee asks, "What should I do if the client says this?" — and you respond from memory. The same explanation every day.
- This is not the employee's failure — it’s the absence of a system. Without an SOP, every hire adds management work to your plate.
- AI takes your usual explanation and organizes it: steps, when, example, exception — you review and test before scaling.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: System → SOP → Testing → People
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Step 1: Write the process as you would explain it to a friend — even if it’s messy.
- Step 2: AI organizes it into an SOP: goal, numbered steps, example, "If this happens."
- Step 3: Test the SOP yourself or with a temporary assistant — adjust what isn’t clear.
- Step 4: Once it works twice with the same quality — consider hiring or delegating.

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: One Term
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| SOP (Standard Operating Procedure) | A fixed way to perform a repetitive task — anyone can follow it | "Respond to price inquiry" — 5 steps + template + when to escalate to the manager |

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: Hiring Without a System vs. SOP First
sections.contentMarkdown:
| People Before System | SOP Then People |
|--------------|------------|
| Each employee works in their own way. You are in the middle — unifying, reviewing, and being reactive | AI helps you document. The employee follows the steps — you only review exceptions |

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: From Raw Explanation to SOP
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Choose one process you explain to yourself often (responding to a client, preparing an order, following up with a supplier). Write it in your own words — then use AI to convert it into an SOP outline (goal, steps, example, exception). Attach the SOP outline in your submission. Submission: Process name · raw explanation (5–10 lines) · SOP outline after AI · one thing that still needs clarification after review. Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Real Process | 60% | Raw explanation from your work — not a generic example |
| Organized SOP | 40% | Outline with clear steps — even if it needs minor adjustments |
